description:
Owner decision item; no code until decided.

Problem. `make pr-arm` reports `outcome: waiting` only when every refusal reason matches WAITING_MARKERS ('waiting for full CI run', 'has not finished for'). Right after a push the reasons are usually mixed. Observed on PR #4098 minutes after a push: the fast-duration verdict was missing because core had not finished (a waiting marker), `required check 'core' completed with conclusion 'failure'` (the placeholder failure from the 'CI (text edit)' run while the real CI run was still in progress), and `review: waiting for the review's verdict`. That combination is `refused`, so `make pr-arm WAIT=<minutes>` (pr-arm-wait-mode-20261111, which by the owner's decision loops only on `waiting`) exits at once in the most common early state and helps only in the later window when the verdict is in and core is still running.

Evidence from 629 `pr-arm: outcome:` lines in 25 reviewed sessions: 141 waiting, 492 refused, 66 armed. Among the refused reasons, about 17 were a pending review verdict, about 35 were waiting markers mixed with another reason, and an unknown share of the 92 'core completed with conclusion failure' lines were placeholders.

Options. (A) Keep it: the wait covers only `waiting`. (B) Inside the wait loop only, also treat a pending review verdict as waiting; without WAIT nothing changes, the wait stays bounded, and arming still needs every gate to pass. (C) B, and also make the visible required-check reason recognise a placeholder failure whose full run for the same head is in progress, as the suite check already does, so the two reasons stop disagreeing.

Guardrails: never change what arms or refuses; a hold, an open review thread, a real failed check or a red trunk must still end the wait at once; never post a stand-in; scripts/pr_arm.py is a soundness path.
